candidate.blueprint_locator: Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies; calculate, administer, and teach individualized insulin therapy safely
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — carbohydrate counting and prandial insulin matching
candidate.educational_objective: Use an individualized insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio to match prandial insulin to meal carbohydrate while incorporating other person-specific factors that can change mealtime insulin needs.

options.A: I estimate the carbohydrate in the meal and use my prescribed ICR to help determine the mealtime insulin dose; I may also need individualized guidance for fat, protein, current glucose, trends, activity, or illness.
options.B: I should give the same mealtime insulin dose every day even when the carbohydrate amount changes substantially.
options.C: Carbohydrate content should be ignored when calculating mealtime insulin because only the fasting glucose determines the dose.
options.D: Using an ICR means I should avoid carbohydrate-containing foods rather than match insulin to the meal.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend teaching most adults with type 1 diabetes to match mealtime insulin to carbohydrate intake and, when relevant, the glycemic effects of fat and protein. Current insulin plans commonly use an individualized insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio for prandial dosing, with additional adjustment based on concurrent glucose, trends, physical activity, illness, and other individualized factors. B and C disconnect mealtime insulin from nutritional needs. D misrepresents carbohydrate counting as carbohydrate avoidance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For adults with type 1 diabetes using flexible prandial insulin, carbohydrate counting and an individualized ICR can guide mealtime insulin dosing, with other meal and clinical factors incorporated as needed.
candidate.source_document_title: Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026; Facilitating Positive Health Behaviors and Well-being to Improve Health Outcomes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026

candidate.stem: An adult with type 1 diabetes uses rapid-acting insulin with meals and an individualized insulin-to-carbohydrate ratio (ICR). Which statement by the client shows correct understanding?
